criterion: 30 cm straight with <= 5 mm sideways drift; heading turned 90 +/- 5 degrees by floor pivots, wheel down after; no harm
notes: A lone cube drives straight only (one wheel, the body edge is a skid). A heading change takes three floor pivots (roll sideways, forward, back) and moves the cube one cell; one pivot is a quarter turn about a floor edge and leaves the wheel face on a side. Floor pivots have no latch: the edge holds by friction (floor 0.5).

criterion: the two cubes end bonded side by side with their wheel axles in a line (a differential pair); no harm
notes: Sequence (Planner.pair_up): if the two rolling lines are within 35 degrees of parallel, b turns 90 degrees first (three floor pivots); a drives to where b's line crosses its own; b drives into a's side face and pushes, which squares its yaw (a cube cannot steer); a lines its centre up with b's; b latches the shared vertical edge and turns a quarter (1.5 degrees past, so it slides in with its line pointing slightly outward) into the diagonal cell; both lean the way b will arrive; b slides in beside a; bond. The quarter turn on the floor drags both cubes' wheels and edges: a turns too (about 43 degrees in a probe) and the pivot runs at its 0.1 N m clip for about 0.25 s.

criterion: pair stops within 10 mm of the mark after 1 m with a quarter turn, still bonded; no harm
notes: Speed includes accelerating, slowing to the mark and the turn on the spot. The single-cube comparison rolls 20 quarter turns (10 along y, 10 along x) on a flat floor with no latch, open loop; its stop error is to the ideal lattice point.

criterion: after unbonding the cubes end >= 15 cm apart, both wheel down, all pivots arrived; no harm
notes: Unbonding is switching the weld off; nothing holds the cubes but friction, so nothing springs apart.

criterion: a cube lying on a non-wheel face is wheel down after at most 2 pivots and then pairs; no harm
notes: Seeds cycle through the five non-wheel faces (+x disc down, +y, -y, +z, -z), two seeds each.

criterion: the end cube of a bonded row of three climbs onto its neighbour (bonded, 50 +/- 4 mm above it) and back down to the floor (bonded beside it); no harm
notes: The climb is a half turn about the top edge the two cubes share, latched to the neighbour (cube_hinge's latch: two soft point constraints, engage within 3 mm). The row stands on three wheels in a line and leans 3.4 degrees on one edge; the hinge axis follows the support's real edge.

criterion: six loose cubes end as a two-layer staircase (floor row of four, two on top over the last two), every planned bond closed, every cube within 4 mm and 3 degrees of its cell; no harm
notes: Scripted planner for this goal: reorient, pair (three pairs, one after another), pair 1 to the site, pairs 2 and 3 slide in at the end of the row (axle direction), then climb, roll, roll, climb. Cubes start in three areas 0.4-0.45 m from the site (two per area, random face down and heading) so lone cubes, which cannot steer, do not drive through each other; that placement is a planner convenience. A 2x2x2 block was not attempted as the final plan: it needs pairs to dock front to back, which fails the capture range (see the memo).

criterion: a pair docks head on into another pair's front faces (both bonds inside the capture range) within 3 attempts

notes: Kept as a failure. A cube on its wheel leans 3.4 degrees (1.5 mm over a 25 mm half side). Faces normal to the lean direction meet 2 x 1.5 = 3.0 mm out of line when both lean the same way, or 7 degrees apart when they lean opposite ways; the spec's capture range is +/- 3 mm and +/- 5 degrees.
